newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin say discount rate up to central bank.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin say discount rate up to central bank.

text.p: Thailand's Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Thursday any discount rate cut was up to the central bank and the ministry had no responsibility over it.
"The discount rate adjustment will be determined by the bank of Thailand, as it deems appropriate," he told reporters.

There had been speculation in the market after a local newspaper report on Tuesday that the Bank of Thailand was likely to cut the discount rate by one percentage point on Wednesday, but it did not materialise.
The discount rate is the interest rate charged to commercial banks on loans from the Bank of Thailand. It currently stands at 10.50 percent.
Amnuay said discount rate is not the only major factor that could bring the commercial banks' lendings rates down as the banks barely borrow from the central bank.

"Any cut in the discount rate will give more of a psychological effect on commercial banks. The Bank of Thailand can send signals (that they want lower rate) through other channels such as the repo rate," Amnuay said, referring to the bond repurchase market.
Thai bank rates are among the highest in the region, with lending rates ranging between 12.75 percent and 13 percent.

Amnuay said earlier this week he would like to see commercial banks lower their interest rates by 200 basis points by the end of the year. He said it was important that the central bank take a lead in making cuts.
